pages.title: MDCache core: subtree map, authority, path traversal, replication and lookup-by-ino

features.name: Subtree-based authority delegation (subtree map)
features.description: Each rank keeps map<CDir*, set<CDir*>> subtrees: dirfrags whose dir_auth != (-1,-2) are delegation points; everything below a subtree root up to its bounds inherits the root's authority. CDir::authority() returns dir_auth on subtree roots, else the inode's authority; CInode::authority() is inode_auth for base inodes, else its parent dentry's dirfrag authority; CDentry::authority() is its dirfrag's.
features.notes: Clients see the result through DirStat.auth/dist and auth caps; admins through 'get subtrees'.

features.name: Ambiguous authority and WAIT_SINGLEAUTH
features.description: dir_auth pairs (a,b) with b != -2 mark migrations, frozen trees (a,a) and resolve; CInode::STATE_AMBIGUOUSAUTH marks inodes moving in cross-rank rename. Requests needing the auth wait WAIT_SINGLEAUTH, hoisted to the subtree root and woken when set_dir_auth makes .second UNKNOWN.
features.notes: Whole-subtree stall during export/import of that subtree.

features.name: Subtree create/merge primitives
features.description: adjust_subtree_auth creates or updates a subtree root and re-parents bounds; try_subtree_merge(_at) merges adjacent subtrees with identical unambiguous dir_auth unless EXPORTBOUND/AUXSUBTREE; adjust_bounded_subtree_auth imposes an exact [root,bounds) region, swallowing intervening subtrees and asserting exact bounds; get_force_dirfrag_bound_set splits local dirfrags to match peer frag bounds.
features.notes: Callers: bootstrap, discover replica decode, Migrator, resolve, journal replay, rename, fragmentation, export pins.

features.name: Subtree map maintenance on directory rename
features.description: Directory rename/rmdir records project_subtree_rename before journaling and adjust_subtree_after_rename after apply; renaming a directory across an authority boundary makes its dirfrags new subtree roots that keep the old authority.
features.notes: POSIX rename semantics are unaffected; authority layout changes.

features.name: Aux subtrees for export pins and fragmentation
features.description: STATE_AUXSUBTREE keeps a dirfrag as its own subtree (no merge) for export pins pinned to this rank and for all-or-none subtree status of dirfrags being fragmented; empty aux subtrees whose inode is auth are dropped by MDCache::trim.
features.notes: Visible to admins through ceph.dir.pin vxattrs and 'get subtrees'. Under mds_thrash_exports, Migrator::export_dir marks the export root itself (not the randomly chosen nested dirfrag) as AUXSUBTREE (src/mds/Migrator.cc:983).

features.name: ESubtreeMap journaling
features.description: create_subtree_map journals all subtrees with dir_auth.first == whoami and their bounds, marks ambiguous imports, applies projected renames, simplifies nested own subtrees, and adds a TO_ROOT spanning tree of dentries/inodes plus each dirfrag fnode; written at every major segment boundary, at boot_create/boot_start, on 'flush journal' and at shutdown.
features.notes: cephfs-journal-tool reads it (C++ format only).

features.name: ESubtreeMap replay
features.description: First ESubtreeMap replayed reconstructs the auth subtree skeleton (adjust_bounded_subtree_auth, ambiguous imports as (me,me)) and recalc_auth_bits; later ones only verify and report mismatches to the cluster log (assert only with mds_debug_subtrees).
features.notes: Cluster log errors reach the monitor.

features.name: Ephemeral pin hashing (jump consistent hash)
features.description: hash_into_rank_bucket(ino, frag) maps a directory (random pin) or dirfrag (distributed pin) to a rank in [0, max_mds) with rjhash64 and the Lamping-Veach jump hash; max_mds changes re-evaluate ephemeral pins and the distributed-pin frag bits.
features.notes: Placement is admin-observable but not a client contract.

features.name: Path traversal with per-component locking (path_traverse)
features.description: Resolves (base ino, relative path) to dentries/inodes: opens or discovers dirfrags, fetches single dentry keys, rdlocks dentry locks (RDLOCK_PATH), xlocks the tail dentry with parent filelock/nestlock wrlocks (XLOCK_DENTRY), rdlocks snaplock chains (RDLOCK_SNAP/SNAP2) and policylocks for layouts (WANT_DIRLAYOUT), attaches lock caches (CHECK_LOCKCACHE), forwards or waits for single auth (WANT_AUTH). Returns 0/1 (waiting)/2 (forwarded)/-errno.
features.notes: Errors seen by clients: ENOENT, ENOTDIR, EINVAL, EIO, ESTALE.

features.name: Snapshot directory traversal
features.description: An empty first path component means .snap (clients encode foo/.snap/bar as foo//bar); the next component is resolved with SnapRealm::resolve_snapname; empty components elsewhere give EINVAL; .snap paths are traversed without path locks and with WANT_AUTH unless the caller passes no_want_auth (readdir, readdir_snapdiff and file_blockdiff do); mutations on .snap paths get EROFS.
features.notes: Snapshots are a Ceph extension; the encoding is a hard client contract.

features.name: Forward to auth and forward-versus-discover heuristic
features.description: A non-auth rank replies MClientRequestForward(dest, num_fwd+1, must_resend); clients resend. If depth < num_fwd of the client request, the rank discovers (replicates) instead of forwarding to stop ping-pong. Batch heads forward the whole batch; internal ops get EXDEV.
features.notes: kclient aborts with EMULTIHOP if fwd_seq does not increase.

features.name: Negative lookup trace (null tail dentry)
features.description: A missing tail name in an auth dirfrag gets a null dentry whenever pdnvec is passed and the snapid is head (rdlocked or xlocked under RDLOCK_PATH/XLOCK_DENTRY); without WANT_DENTRY the traversal returns ENOENT with that dentry in pdnvec, and rdlock_path_pin_ref puts it in the ENOENT reply trace when the client wants the dentry, enabling negative dentry leases.
features.notes: Negative caching is an optimization; ENOENT itself is POSIX.

features.name: Hard-link target resolution
features.description: Remote dentries (remote_ino, d_type) are linked to the cached target or resolved by open_remote_dentry -> open_ino (want_replica); failure marks the dentry BADREMOTEINO, records DamageTable remote damage (rank goes damaged past mds_damage_table_max_entries), traversal returns EIO and readdir omits the entry.
features.notes: POSIX link(2) requires resolving any name to the shared inode.

features.name: Damage-aware traversal
features.description: Traversal returns EIO for dirfrags or dentries recorded in the DamageTable and for remote inodes marked damaged, and refuses to fetch damaged dirfrags.

features.name: Discover protocol (pull replication)
features.description: MDiscover/MDiscoverReply replicate base inodes, dirfrags, dentries (including null ones) and inodes along a path from the auth; tracked by tid, deduplicated by waiter presence, re-sent by kick_discovers when a peer reaches REJOIN+; the auth stops at frozen/xlocked/unfetched items, gives dir_auth hints, and defers discovers from survivors while rejoining.

features.name: Replica codec with nonces
features.description: encode/decode_replica_{dir,dentry,inode,stray} carry base state, replica lock states (applied only on creation), need_recover, alternate_name and per-recipient nonces; the auth's replica_map[rank] holds the last nonce and MCacheExpire with a stale nonce is ignored; EXPORT_NONCE=1 on migration.

features.name: Replica subtrees at delegation boundaries
features.description: decode_replica_dir makes a newly replicated dirfrag a non-auth subtree root (dir_auth = sender) when the sender differs from the inode's authority, the inode is ambiguous, or the inode is a base inode; non-auth subtree roots are removed when trimmed.

features.name: Push link/unlink to replicas
features.description: After applying a new link (openc, mknod/mkdir/symlink, link, rename) the auth sends MDentryLink with an inode replica or remote link to dentry replica holders (skipping witnesses and recovering ranks); unlink/rmdir send MDentryUnlink with a per-recipient stray replica chain; replicas relink the inode under the stray, adjust subtrees and export their client caps to the auth.
features.notes: Relies on replicas not trimming unreadable dentries and per-peer FIFO ordering with MLock.

features.name: Directory replication hint and client dist
features.description: dir_rep REP_NONE/ALL/LIST with MDirUpdate broadcast to active non-holders: MDBalancer::hit_dir, once per sample period for read hits on an auth unambiguous dirfrag with can_rep(), sets REP_ALL when pop_auth_subtree + 10*pop_me >= mds_bal_replicate_threshold (8000); unreplication below mds_bal_unreplicate_threshold (default 0) never fires by default. Replies carry DirStat{frag, auth=dir_auth.first (-1 if not a subtree root), dist=replica holders+self when auth and replicated} unless mds_forward_all_requests_to_auth.
features.notes: Clients use dist to send read requests to random replicas.

features.name: Lookup by inode number (open_ino)
features.description: open_ino locates any inode by number: coalesces concurrent opens, asks peer caches (MMDSOpenIno), fetches the RADOS backtrace, traverses ancestors (fetching keys or discovering), recursively opens parents; completes with the auth rank or an error. Used by LOOKUPINO/LOOKUPHASH/LOOKUPPARENT/LOOKUPNAME, ESTALE recovery, hard links, rejoin cap import and OpenFileTable prefetch.
features.notes: NFS file handles (kclient export ops, Ganesha) and kclient quota realm lookups depend on it; stalls while any 'in' rank is not active.

features.name: Backtrace-based inode location
features.description: fetch_backtrace reads xattr 'parent' (inode_backtrace_t: ino, ancestors (dirino,dname,version), pool, old_pools) from <ino>.00000000 in the default data pool, following bt.pool redirects and falling back to the metadata pool on ENOENT; empty backtrace -> ESTALE, same parent twice -> EINVAL, decode error -> EIO.
features.notes: On-disk format of the C++ MDS; cephfs-data-scan reads backtraces.

features.name: open_ino peer protocol
features.description: MMDSOpenIno(tid, ino, ancestors) asks one peer at a time (auth hint first); the peer replies with the full ancestor chain if auth, an auth hint if it has a replica, or the result of its own non-discovering ancestor traversal; replies from a rank other than the one being checked are ignored.

features.name: Batched dentry-key fetches for open_ino
features.description: While open_ino_batch is set (rejoin cap import, OpenFileTable prefetch), single-key fetches are grouped per dirfrag into one fetch_keys OMAP read.

features.name: ESTALE recovery via find_ino_peers
features.description: When a request's base inode is not cached, ask each active peer (MMDSFindIno) for a path to it, discover that path, and retry; if every peer fails, fall back to open_ino and forward the client request to the returned rank; ENOENT/ENODATA become ESTALE for the client.
features.notes: Clients do not retry ESTALE; the server-side search is the only recovery.

features.name: Foreign mdsdir and stray base resolution
features.description: Paths based on another rank's ~mdsN are opened by discovering the base inode from that rank; paths based on a foreign stray inode are rewritten as stray<i> under ~mdsN and discovered.
features.notes: Used by cross-rank rename/rmdir and stray handling.

features.name: Private inode numbers refused for LOOKUPINO
features.description: LOOKUPINO/LOOKUPHASH/LOOKUPPARENT/LOOKUPNAME of ~mdsN, stray or log inode numbers (MDS_IS_PRIVATE_INO) return ESTALE; purging inodes return ESTALE.

features.name: Cache-only path resolution for admin commands
features.description: cache_traverse walks the in-memory cache only (no IO, locks or waits) from an ino, ~mdsdir/~mdsN or the root; used by export dir, dump tree, dirfrag split/merge/ls and dump dir.

features.name: 'get subtrees' admin command
features.description: Dumps every subtree: is_auth, auth_first, auth_second, export_pin, distributed/random ephemeral pin flags, export_pin_target and the full CDir dump.
features.notes: Consumed by qa tests and operators.

features.name: Resend on peer state changes
features.description: Outstanding discovers, open_ino peer queries and find_ino queries have no timeouts; they are re-sent or restarted when a peer reaches REJOIN+ or fails (kick_discovers, kick_open_ino_peers, kick_find_ino_peers).
features.notes: Driven by MDSMap updates from the monitor.

features.name: Lock-cache attach and async-dirop flush during traversal
features.description: CHECK_LOCKCACHE attaches a client's lock cache on the base dir; non-xlocking traversals wrlock the parent filelock when a lock cache holds it, forcing invalidation so clients flush async creates/unlinks before others read.
features.notes: See leases-lock-caches-and-async-dirops page.

features.name: Traversal perf counters
features.description: mds.traverse, traverse_hit, traverse_forward, traverse_discover, traverse_dir_fetch, traverse_remote_ino, traverse_lock, openino_dir_fetch, openino_backtrace_fetch, openino_peer_discover, subtrees gauge, forward; mds_cache.dir_update, dir_update_receipt, dir_try_discover, dir_send_discover, dir_handle_discover.
features.notes: Exported through the mgr prometheus module like other MDS counters.

features.name: Replica lock-state propagation via MLock
features.description: After creation, replicas receive lock state and lock-protected data only through MLock messages (e.g. LOCK_AC_SYNC with encode_locked_state); send_lock_message sends to every replica_map holder, skipping holders below REJOIN while the cluster is degraded. Replica blobs carry lock replica states (s16) that are applied only when the replica object is created.
features.notes: Replica readability of dentries depends on this; see the lock state machine page.

features.name: dir_auth transitions during subtree migration
features.description: Exporter: freeze (me,me), export sent (me,dest), ack (dest,me), notify acks (dest,-2), abort (me,me)->(me,-2). Importer: prep bounded (oldauth,me), MExportDir (me,oldauth), finish (me,me)->(me,-2), abort (oldauth,-2). Bystanders apply bounded new_auth from MExportDirNotify. Replay produces only (me,me) for journaled ambiguous imports and (-2,-2) for exported subtrees.
features.notes: Visible to admins as auth_first/auth_second in 'get subtrees'.

serialization_points.name: Subtree map edits
serialization_points.why_serialized: Single per-rank map mutated under mds_lock by migration, resolve, replay, rename, fragmentation, discover decode and export pins; traversals read it implicitly through get_subtree_root/authority().
serialization_points.notes: Only the affected subtree, its parent and its bounds actually change.

serialization_points.name: WAIT_SINGLEAUTH hoisted to subtree root
serialization_points.shared_state: waiter list of the subtree root dirfrag
serialization_points.why_serialized: Any request needing the auth of any object in an ambiguous subtree waits until the whole subtree becomes single-auth.
serialization_points.notes: During export the whole tree is frozen (me,me); per-object migration would shrink the scope.

serialization_points.name: Freeze tree for export
serialization_points.shared_state: auth pins and freeze state of every dirfrag in the exported subtree
serialization_points.why_serialized: Export requires a quiescent subtree; forces (me,me) ambiguous auth.

serialization_points.name: path_traverse cache walk
serialization_points.shared_state: CDir::items maps, inode_map, dentry lock states, LRU
serialization_points.why_serialized: Runs entirely under mds_lock; acquires rdlocks/xlocks per component via Locker::acquire_locks.
serialization_points.notes: Real conflicts are the dentry rdlock vs xlock and parent filelock/nestlock wrlocks.

serialization_points.name: Global inode index
serialization_points.why_serialized: Single container for all cached inodes of the rank.

serialization_points.name: Discover tracking and dedup
serialization_points.shared_state: discovers map, discover_last_tid, dir/dentry waiter lists
serialization_points.why_serialized: Per-rank tid counter and waiter-based dedup under mds_lock.

serialization_points.name: Replica bookkeeping
serialization_points.why_serialized: Nonce increments and expire validation must be consistent per object.

serialization_points.name: MDentryLink/MDentryUnlink versus MLock ordering
serialization_points.why_serialized: Replicas rely on the link/unlink message arriving before the lock SYNC that makes the dentry readable again, and on not trimming unreadable dentries.
serialization_points.notes: Any replicated design needs per-object ordering of update and invalidation messages.

serialization_points.name: open_ino coalescing and sequential peer search
serialization_points.why_serialized: One state machine per ino; peers are asked one at a time; the search waits until all 'in' ranks are active.
serialization_points.notes: Peer queries could be parallel; waiting for all ranks is a design choice.

serialization_points.name: find_ino_peers sequential search
serialization_points.why_serialized: One peer at a time per request.

serialization_points.name: open_ino batch flag
serialization_points.why_serialized: Rank-global batching window for key fetches during rejoin/OFT prefetch.

serialization_points.name: create_subtree_map snapshot
serialization_points.shared_state: whole subtree map, projected_subtree_renames, ambiguous imports, journaler expire_pos
serialization_points.why_serialized: ESubtreeMap must describe the complete auth partition of the rank's single journal at the segment boundary.
serialization_points.notes: With per-shard journals only the shard's own state needs snapshotting.

serialization_points.name: ESubtreeMap replay
serialization_points.shared_state: subtree map and cache during replay

serialization_points.name: DamageTable checks
serialization_points.why_serialized: Lookups on a shared table during traversal.

serialization_points.name: Peer-search barrier on the MDSMap in set
serialization_points.why_serialized: Both open_ino and find_ino_peers refuse to move on (to the backtrace or to ESTALE) until every 'in' rank other than self has been asked, so one non-active rank stalls every uncached lookup-by-ino and ESTALE recovery on every rank.
serialization_points.notes: Also src/mds/MDCache.cc:9672 (MDCache::_do_find_ino_peer). A stale auth_hint naming a non-active rank keeps open_ino waiting even when other peers are available.

external_contract.detail: Non-auth rank sends MClientRequestForward(tid, dest, num_fwd+1, client_must_resend=true); kernel resends to dest, aborting with EMULTIHOP if fwd_seq <= r_num_fwd.

Reply traces and readdir carry DirStat{frag, auth (-1 = same as dir inode auth cap), dist (replicas+auth, only from auth when replicated)}; kclient keeps up to 4 dist entries and may send USE_ANY_MDS requests to a random replica, else to auth.
Paths through .snap are sent relative to the nearest non-snapshot ancestor with .snap encoded as an empty component (foo//bar); the MDS accepts it only as the first component (EINVAL otherwise).

external_contract.item: Lookup by inode number from any rank
external_contract.detail: LOOKUPINO (NFS file handles, quota realm inodes, snapdir stat), LOOKUPPARENT, LOOKUPNAME are sent with USE_ANY_MDS; any rank must locate the inode cluster-wide and reply or forward; ESTALE goes to the caller.

external_contract.item: Dentry name hash for frag/MDS choice
external_contract.detail: Clients hash names with the directory's dir_layout.dl_dir_hash (0 = Linux dcache hash, default rjenkins 2) to pick the frag and MDS; the MDS uses the same function to pick dirfrags.
For lookups that want the dentry, an ENOENT reply carries the null tail dentry with a lease when the tail dirfrag is auth.
update_dir_dist records DirStat.auth >= 0 in fragmap and dist in frag_repmap only when the reply came from DirStat.auth; DirStat.frag forces client fragtree leaves.
make_nosnap_relative_path pushes an empty dentry for the snapdir.
_lookup_vino sends LOOKUPINO to rand() % num_in_mds; lookup_hash/_lookup_parent/_lookup_name use LOOKUPHASH/LOOKUPPARENT/LOOKUPNAME.
FSAL_CEPH resolves handles with ceph_ll_lookup_inode -> LOOKUPINO, needing cluster-wide lookup by ino.
getxattr 'parent' on <ino hex>.00000000 in the default data pool, bt.pool, or metadata pool; single-key OMAP reads of dirfrag objects <ino hex>.<frag hex> in the metadata pool.
Array of subtrees with is_auth, auth_first, auth_second, export_pin, distributed_ephemeral_pin, random_ephemeral_pin, export_pin_target, dir (CDir::dump).
export dir, dump tree, dirfrag split/merge/ls, dump dir resolve paths with cache_traverse and fail if not cached.

ENOENT (missing/null/purging dentry, unknown snapshot), ENOTDIR, EINVAL (misplaced snapdir, stale backtrace twice), EIO (damage), ESTALE (unknown/purging base inode, private ino), EROFS (mutation through .snap).

rust_implications.implication: C++ authority is a subtree map of dirfrag delegation points with inheritance; a Rust Shard Manager can use shard roots with stable identity instead, but must still expose a consistent per-dirfrag auth rank to clients (DirStat.auth/dist) and per-inode auth (auth caps), and must forward requests that land on a non-owner rank with MClientRequestForward and an increasing num_fwd.

C++ hoists WAIT_SINGLEAUTH to the subtree root and freezes entire subtrees for export; per-shard 2PC migration should fence only the migrating shard and queue or forward requests for it, leaving siblings untouched.

Clients work if every rank returns empty dist and forwards non-owned requests; C++ replication (discover, MDentryLink/Unlink, MLock SYNC data) exists to let non-auth ranks traverse paths and serve reads. A Rust MDS can avoid general replication by forwarding at shard boundaries, at the cost of extra client round trips for paths crossing shards; if read replicas are added, update/invalidate ordering per object (like MDentryLink before MLock SYNC) is required.

rust_implications.topic: Path-relative requests need cross-shard name resolution
rust_implications.implication: kclient sends (base ino, relative path) and may choose any rank via dist/caps; the receiving shard must resolve components owned by other shards (forward to owner of the first non-owned component, or a cross-shard lookup service). Use the num_fwd heuristic or equivalent to prevent forward ping-pong.

LOOKUPINO/LOOKUPPARENT/LOOKUPNAME may arrive at any rank (NFS handles, Ganesha, kclient quota realms). C++ searches peer caches then reads backtraces from the data pool and stalls while any rank is down. A Rust MDS should keep an authoritative ino -> (parent, shard) index in its own RADOS format (or encode the owning shard in ino ranges) so the owner is found in O(1) and per shard, also in degraded clusters.

Remote dentries need efficient target resolution (readdir includes target attributes; C++ omits unresolvable entries). An inode table keyed by ino, decoupled from dentries, removes the need for backtraces and stray-based primary relocation.

ESubtreeMap is a rank-global snapshot plus a spanning tree of ancestor dentries needed because events only journal context up to the nearest auth subtree root. With per-shard journals and an ino-indexed store, each shard checkpoint need only describe that shard; no ancestor spanning tree is required for replay.

rust_implications.topic: Traversal locking maps to hierarchical locks
rust_implications.implication: path_traverse takes rdlocks on every traversed dentry, rdlocks snaplock on every ancestor (snaprealm/quota stability), policylock up to the nearest layout, and for creates xlocks the tail dentry plus wrlocks parent filelock/nestlock (and rdlock authlock). In an S/X/IS/IX manager this becomes IS on ancestors and S on traversed dentries, IX on the parent dir plus X on the new dentry; same-directory creates of different names then commute.

rust_implications.topic: Snapdir encoding is a hard contract
rust_implications.implication: Parse decoded paths keeping empty components; treat only the first empty component as .snap, return EINVAL otherwise, EROFS for mutations through .snap.
Return the null tail dentry with a lease on ENOENT when the client wants the dentry, to keep kclient negative dentry caching effective.
ceph.dir.pin.distributed/random semantics depend on hashing (ino, frag) over max_mds; reusing rjhash64 + jump consistent hash keeps placement familiar but exact placement is not a client contract.

rust_implications.topic: No timeouts in C++ MDS-to-MDS lookups
rust_implications.implication: C++ discovers/open_ino/find_ino have no timeouts and rely on MDSMap changes to resend; Rust inter-shard RPCs should have explicit retry/timeout and idempotent request ids.
Neither kclient nor libcephfs retries ESTALE; the Rust MDS must exhaust its own lookup mechanism (index, owner shard) before returning ESTALE, and map not-found to ESTALE for lookup-by-ino.
Reject lookup-by-ino of internal inodes (journal, stray, mdsdir equivalents) with ESTALE as C++ does for MDS_IS_PRIVATE_INO.
MDentryUnlink.snapbl is never encoded, C_MDC_RetryDiscoverPath passes a rank as a bool, handle_dentry_link aborts on missing dentries; these are internal to C++ and need not be mimicked.

open_questions: Is the discover_path(CInode*) branch with from == whoami (which leaks the onfinish context) reachable in practice? path_traverse only calls it for !is_auth() inodes that are not ambiguous, so it needs authority().first == whoami with the auth bit clear.

C_MDC_RetryDiscoverPath::finish passes 'from' as the bool path_locked argument (confirmed in code); is the resulting path-locked re-discover ever harmful (it lets the auth replicate xlocked dentries and a frozen tail)?
Can open_ino hang indefinitely when auth_hint names a rank that has stopped (do_open_ino_peer asks nobody else and keeps the hint until it is used)? Not verified at runtime.
MDentryUnlink.snapbl is never encoded; are replica snaprealms for unlinked directories always fixed up by another path (MMDSSnapUpdate, rmdir witness prep), or can they diverge?
MDirUpdate broadcast excludes existing replica holders, leaving their dir_rep stale; is anything besides client dist affected?
Do any production tools besides qa tests consume the 'get subtrees' JSON?
Under mds_thrash_exports, Migrator::export_dir marks the export root rather than the chosen nested dirfrag as AUXSUBTREE; is that a test-only bug or intended?
